concepts.learning_objective: Explain why macroeconomics can study the whole economy through aggregate variables and a single representative good.
Distinguish microeconomic questions and agents from macroeconomic ones.
Explain why macroeconomics sometimes divides the economy into a few distinct goods or sectors.

topics.title: Economic agents and why macroeconomics is needed

concepts.learning_objective: Define economic agents and identify consumers, producers and institutions as examples.
State the reasons economists had to look beyond Adam Smith's self-interest view of markets.
Identify macroeconomic decision-makers such as the State, RBI and SEBI and the public goals they pursue.
Describe the classical view of full employment that dominated economics before Keynes.
Describe the Great Depression of 1929 and calculate the unemployment rate from its definition.
Explain how Keynes's General Theory (1936) gave rise to macroeconomics as a separate branch.

topics.title: The capitalist economy and its firms

concepts.learning_objective: State the features of a capitalist economy and recognise economies to which they do not apply.
Match the factors of production with rent, interest, wages and profit.
Identify investment expenditure as spending that raises productive capacity.
Define a household and explain how households earn incomes and support firms' markets.
Describe the economic functions of the government sector.
Explain exports, imports and capital flows as links with the external sector.
